system_prompt_style.evidence_quote:
Prefix: """ You are the Controller Agent, responsible for
processing an input query related to Control Theory.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: You will be provided with both the question and a predefined execution plan, detailing the sequence of tools you should use to arrive at the final answer.
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/codebase environment; optional RAG Retriever over user-provided documents (embedding_rag-like) reachable, see Sec. 3.1.

context_compaction.note: Pseudocode accumulates messages without compaction; paper mentions 'efficient memory handling' via Memory Agent but no compaction mechanism described.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Observation: System Type: TF, Objective: step_response, Ordered Tools: ['control.tf', 'control.step_response'].
observation_format.note: Plots are generated as figures but shown as <TimeResponseData> object text to the agent.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
Action: the action to take, should be one of {agent_tools}.
Action Input: the input to the action.
tool_call_format.evidence_locator: paper App. A, Format Instruction Prompt
tool_call_format.note: ReAct-style text action parsing; closest allowed value is json_in_text (structured key:value in text), not native function calling.

tool_count.evidence_quote: features a Controller Agent at its core, equipped with more than 140 tools.
tool_count.note: Controller Agent tool count; auxiliary agents have their own smaller tool sets.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: We categorize these functions, serving as tools for the Controller Agent, into four categories: system representation, controller analysis, controller design, and simulation
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; tools are control-library functions.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: tool descriptions are provided through the tool functions, not the prompts

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: we propose using existing library packages as a comprehensive tools package, leveraging the vast number of specialized libraries available.
protocol_standardization.note: No mention of MCP or A2A anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
Thought: you should always think about what to do.
Action: the action to take
loop_primitives.evidence_locator: paper App. A, Format Instruction Prompt
loop_primitives.note: Planner produces a plan before Controller executes; Critic feedback triggers refinement (critique-repair loop).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the Supervisor passes the query to the Planner Agent, which organizes the sequence of functions (or tools) that the Controller Agent will use to generate the response.
planning_granularity.note: Plan is an ordered tool list passed to the Controller.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a supervisor LLM acts as the central decision-maker, orchestrating a network of specialized LLM agents to optimize task execution and workflow efficiency.

delegation_mechanism.note: Control passes between agent nodes in a shared message list graph.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
Action: human_tool
Action Input: Please identify the format you prefer for the output file.
human_in_loop.note: Communicator Agent has a Human-in-the-loop tool used at delivery time.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The framework also features memory capabilities, enabling it to recall past conversations, user priorities, and personalized preferences
long_term_memory.note: Memory Agent stores/recalls whole conversations; storage backend not specified.

state_persistence.note: No resume/checkpoint path described in the pseudocode.

self_verification.evidence_quote: the Critic Agent, a trusted judge [29], reviews it to ensure alignment with the original user query. If the answer does not meet the necessary criteria, the Critic Agent provides feedback for improvement

retry_policy.evidence_quote: prompting the Controller Agent to refine the response. If the answer is validated, it is stored efficiently by the Memory Agent
retry_policy.note: Retry loop driven by Critic acceptance; no fixed cap reported.

rollback.evidence_quote: the Controller Agent consults the Debugger Agent for troubleshooting guidance before proceeding.

termination_condition.note: Loop ends when routing reaches END; no step/token/cost caps reported.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: By disabling unnecessary services from specific agents, the model can be made more cost-effective for real-world applications.
cost_controls.note: Costs are measured but no budget, caching or routing mechanism is implemented.

timeouts.evidence_quote: all task runtimes under 25 seconds and the monetary cost per task below $0.002
timeouts.note: Runtimes reported; no timeout enforcement described.

execution_isolation.note: Python-REPL and control-library tools appear to run in-process; no isolation described. Compute: 2vCPU @ 2.2GHz.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote:
Retriever
File Reader
Directory Finder
Retriever Agent
filesystem_access.note: File reader / directory finder tools with no stated path restriction; coded relative to the host process.

network_policy.evidence_quote: the Researcher Agent can search the internet for relevant information

permission_model.evidence_quote: Once the planning is complete, the Controller Agent, positioned at the heart of the system, executes the necessary functions to construct the answer.
permission_model.note: No allowlist or approval step before action execution.

tracing.evidence_quote: The verbose outputs from all agents are shown to reveal the intermediate reasoning steps of the LLM-Agent-Controller.

replayability.evidence_quote: To reduce randomness in the performance metrics, the system was run 20 times for each category.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: we establish several metrics to quantitatively evaluate various performance aspects
eval_hooks.note: Metrics defined in the paper; no shipped evaluation runner, code is not public.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the reinforcement of robustness and safety for critical applications
guardrails.note: Safety guardrails listed as future work.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system developed to address a wide range of problems in control engineering (Control Theory)
target_domain.note: Domain is control engineering; no listed value fits, closest is other.

open_source.evidence_quote: All of the robots’ codes are available in the archive of the Social & Cognitive Robotics Laboratory.
open_source.note: Code available on request only, no public repo.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: The performance evaluation of the LLM-Agent-Controller system across ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Detailed information about the tools, including their descriptions, network graph, and parser functions, is available upon request

first_release_date.evidence_quote: LLM-Agent-Controller: A Universal Multi-Agent Large Language Model System as a Control Engineer
first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv v1 posting date inferred from identifier 2505; no release tag exists.

pinned_version.evidence_quote: LLM-Agent-Controller: A Universal Multi-Agent Large Language Model System as a Control Engineer
pinned_version.note: No repo to pin; paper is the artifact.
